claim: Réserve Africaine de Sigean charges €34 adult and €24 child (4–14) for single-entry tickets; family pack drops to €31/€21; disabled visitors €14.50.
quote: Adults: €34; Children (4-14 years): €24. Family Pack (2 adults + 3+ children): Adults €31, Children €21. Disabled visitors receive a reduced rate of €14.50 with written proof.

claim: The reserve opens daily from 9 a.m. year-round (8:30 a.m. in peak summer 6 Jul–31 Aug 2026); last admission varies 4 PM (winter) to 5 PM (summer).
quote: Open Every Day, from 9 a.m. ... 8:30 a.m. from 6 July to 31 August 2026. Mar 29 – Jul 5: last admission 5 PM; Oct 26 – Mar 28: last admission 4 PM.

claim: Sigean hosts more than 3,800 animals across nearly 300 hectares with a drive-through section (lions, Tibetan bears, giraffes, rhinos) and a pedestrian section (chimps, alligators, 1,000+ birds including flamingos).
quote: More than 3,800 animals live in almost 300 hectares of woods, lagoons and 'garrigue'. Visits include a drive through the enclosure with lions, Tibetan bears, giraffes and rhinoceroses and a pedestrian tour to meet dromedaries, chimpanzees, alligators, and more than 1000 birds.

claim: A signed 7.5 km loop from the Mairie de Fontjoncouse to the Saint-Victor hermitage and back takes about 3 h with 293 m of elevation gain, rated moderate.
quote: 7,5 km ... 3h ... 293 m ... Modérée ... Mairie de Fontjoncouse, Avenue de Saint-Victor ... l'ermitage Saint-Victor et la table d'orientation.

claim: An alternative longer loop to Pic Saint-Victor from Fontjoncouse runs ~11 km with +482 m and roughly 4 h 30, parking at Avenue du Ripaud at the village entrance.
quote: approximately 11.04 km with a vertical gain of +482 m and a calculated time of 4h 30 with moderate difficulty. Parking is available at the entrance to the village of Fontjoncouse, Avenue du Ripaud.

claim: The Pic Saint-Victor summit carries a thousand-year-old pre-Romanesque hermitage chapel (former Fontfroide-dissident monks' chapel) and two orientation tables with views over the lakes, Mediterranean and Pyrenees to the Luchonnais peaks.
quote: thousand-year-old hermitage, the former chapel of the dissident monks of Fontfroide Abbey ... two orientation tables: one to the west and the other to the south-east ... view of the lakes and the sea, as well as the Pyrenees mountain range stretching to the peaks of Luchonnais.

claim: Mont Tauch peaks at 917 m at Pech de Fraysse; the summit's Tower of Geographers was built in 1791 by Delambre and Méchain to measure the Dunkirk–Barcelona meridian and offers a 360° panorama of the Mediterranean and Cathar castles.
quote: 917 meters at Pech de Fraysse ... Tower of Geographers at the summit was constructed in 1791 by astronomers including Jean-Baptiste Delambre and Pierre Méchain to measure the meridian from Dunkirk to Barcelona ... grand panorama of the Mediterranean and Cathar castles.

claim: The Tour de la Montagne du Tauch is a 60 km multi-day loop typically done over 3 days, with a summer shuttle from Tuchan (9 a.m./11 a.m./4 p.m. daily in July–August, weekends in June and September) for those skipping the full ascent.
quote: 60 km hiking itinerary can be completed in 3 days ... shuttle service is set up daily in July and August at 9am, 11am and 4pm, and on Saturdays and Sundays in June and September at 9am, 11am and 4pm to access the Mont Tauch summit.

claim: The Sentier Cathare Étape 2 runs from Durban-Corbières to Tuchan, paralleling the scenic D611 valley road through vineyards and garrigue.
quote: LE SENTIER CATHARE, ÉTAPE 02 : DE DURBAN À TUCHAN ... DURBAN-CORBIERES

claim: Aude is one of France's windiest departments with 300–350 days of wind per year; the tramontane (NW) is dominant and most aggressive October to February with gusts reaching ~140 km/h.
quote: 300 to 350 days of wind per year, and the Tramontane is a strong wind that plagues this area during October through to February ... gusts of up to one hundred and forty kilometers per hour and can be dry and cold.

claim: Tramontane episodes in the Aude routinely trigger Météo-France orange weather alerts, signalling conditions hazardous enough to disrupt exposed outdoor plans.
quote: Aude placed under orange weather alert for high winds thanks to tramontane

claim: The Étang de Bages-Sigean stretches 14 km north–south over 5,000+ hectares, hosts ~200 bird species (including ~5,000 flamingos) and has signed loops from Bages, Peyriac-de-Mer, Sigean and Port-la-Nouvelle.
quote: stretches 14 kilometers from north to south, covering an area of over 5,000 hectares ... Nearly 200 species of migratory or sedentary birds ... approximately 5,000 flamingos ... short loops departing from Sigean, Bages, Peyriac-de-Mer, Port-la-Nouvelle and Narbonne.

claim: Location Vélos Peyriac (Peyriac-de-Mer, ~25 km from Fontjoncouse) rents e-bikes by the day, weekend or week for exploring Bages, Gruissan, Île Sainte-Lucie and the Corbières.
quote: This family-owned business rents e-bikes for exploring the area including Peyriac, Bages, Gruissan, Ile-Sainte-Lucie, Narbonne, and the Corbières. They offer daily rentals, weekend options, and weekly rentals.
